jobs.title: Advisor, Human Resources (Red Lake, ON, CA)
jobs.description:
The Great Bear project is a development-stage asset located in the renowned and prolific Red Lake mining district, and represents one of the most exciting recent gold discoveries globally.  The project has excellent potential to become a top-tier deposit that could support a large, long-life mine complex. Kinross’ comprehensive exploration and development program will aim to support the vision of a quality, high-grade, open-pit mine and a longer-term, sizeable underground mine.

Job Summary

Reporting to the Business Partner, Human Resources, the Advisor, Human Resources provides front-line Human Resources advisory and support to employees, supervisors, and site leaders across the Great Bear Project. This role supports employee relations, disciplinary and fact-finding meetings, investigations, attendance and performance management, policy interpretation, workforce administration, payroll support, onboarding, training coordination, and employee lifecycle processes. The Advisor, Human Resources helps leaders apply Human Resources programs consistently, address workplace issues early, and maintain a safe, compliant, and productive work environment during the transition from construction to operations.

Key Responsibilities and Duties

Provide front-line HR advice to employees, supervisors, and site leaders on policy interpretation, employee inquiries, workforce administration, and day-to-day employee relations matters.

Support employee relations activities, including disciplinary interviews, fact-finding meetings, investigations, attendance management, performance management, accommodation and return-to-work processes, and related documentation.

Gather information, prepare interview questions, participate in meetings, document findings, identify risks, and escalate complex or sensitive employee relations matters to the Business Partner, Human Resources as required.

Coach supervisors and site leaders on performance expectations, progressive discipline, attendance standards, respectful workplace practices, and preparation for difficult employee conversations.

Maintain Human Resource Information System (HRIS) records and support HR data accuracy through regular audits, reporting, and record maintenance.

Maintain accurate and confidential employee files and records in accordance with Company standards and applicable privacy requirements.

Support site payroll administration, including time and attendance review, discrepancy follow-up, employee payroll inquiries, and coordination with payroll resources to ensure accurate and timely processing.

Administer employee life cycle transactions, including benefits, leaves of absence, employee status changes, onboarding records, and related documentation.

Coordinate and deliver HR onboarding, orientation, employee communications, and training-related support.

Assist with the development, implementation, and administration of HR policies, procedures, and programs while ensuring compliance with applicable legislation and Company standards.

Assist the Business Partner, Human Resources and Human Resources leadership team with audits, projects, reporting requirements, workforce initiatives, and continuous improvement activities.

Build and maintain positive working relationships with employees, supervisors, contractors, and site leadership to support employee engagement and a positive workplace culture.

Attend crew meetings and site meetings as required to communicate Human Resources programs, provide employee support, and address routine Human Resources concerns.

.

Support Human Resources service delivery during the transition from construction to operations, coordinating with Talent Acquisition, Health and Safety, Security, and site leadership as required.

Ensure strict confidentiality and privacy surrounding all company and employee information.

Work in a healthy work environment with full support, cooperation, and commitment to satisfy our operation’s goal of being accident-free.

Support a work environment that is aligned with Kinross’ Safeground principles.

Comply with federal and provincial acts and regulations, and legal requirements.

Adhere to all relevant Great Bear policies and procedures.

Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

Post-secondary education in Human Resources, Business Administration, Industrial Relations, or a related discipline, combined with 2 to 5 years of progressive Human Resources experience in a Human Resources Advisor, Human Resources Generalist, or similar role.

Experience should include employee relations, disciplinary meetings, workplace investigations, attendance management, performance management, policy interpretation, payroll or Human Resources administration support, and direct support to supervisors or operational leaders. Experience in mining, construction, industrial, remote sites, or project-based environment is considered an asset.

CPHR designation or working toward certification is considered an asset.

Proficient computer skills and experience using HRIS, payroll, and employee data systems; experience with JDE and SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central is considered an asset.

Strong verbal, written, analytical, and persuasive skills, with the ability to build credibility and interact effectively with employees, supervisors, contractors, and management.

Working knowledge of Ontario employment legislation, human rights obligations, privacy requirements, workplace accommodation principles, and HR best practices.

Demonstrated ability to assess employee relations issues, ask effective fact-finding questions, document matters clearly, identify risks, and know when to escalate to the Business Partner, Human Resources or Human Resources leadership.

Comfortable coaching supervisors through employee conversations, attendance concerns, performance expectations, progressive discipline, and respectful workplace matters.

High attention to detail with excellent organizati

jobs.title: Maintenance Dispatcher (Elko, NV, US)
jobs.description:
Bald Mountain is an open-pit mine with a large estimated mineral resource in the largest private mining land package in the U.S. The mine is located in White Pine County, one of the best mining jurisdictions in the world, along the southern extension of the prolific Carlin trend. Bald Mountain and the nearby Round Mountain mine make up Kinross’ Nevada operations. 

Bald Mountain is an important contributor to the economy of northeastern Nevada and maintains a comprehensive environmental strategy including wildlife protection, habitat recovery and education.

Job Description

The successful candidate will work under the direction and supervision of the Planning Supervisor while coordinating with Operations Dispatch/personnel and the Mobile Maintenance team to achieve daily availability and tonnage targets. A successful candidate will work as a maintenance dispatcher on a rotating shift with an assigned Maintenance crew (Days only).  Tasks include using Machine Health Systems (MyCat, MyKomatsu, Prevail and E-global) to identify equipment issues before functional failure, generating reports, creating maintenance work orders and keeping an accurate equipment down list using Dispatch Systems. Working closely with the Maintenance crew by communicating equipment needs and helping Mine Operations meet daily tonnage targets in support of the mine plan. The successful candidate will act with professionalism and integrity as a representative of Kinross.   

Job Responsibilities

•    Work in an office environment for 12.5 hour rotating shifts.
•    Two way radio interaction with personnel
•    Use analytical skills and tools to identify potential equipment issues.
•    Properly address equipment critical alarms.
•    Keep an accurate and detailed list of downed equipment.
•    Support supervisors dispatching field mechanics to ensure safe and efficient production.
•    Create maintenance work orders.
•    Coordinate with Mine Operations to ensure scheduled equipment delivery time compliance.
•    Generate daily and weekly reports to support the reliability decisions.
•    Demonstrate the willingness to learn and apply procedures applicable to position. 

Qualification and Skill Requirements

•    Required: Minimum of 1 year experience working for a mining operation (Preferable maintenance background)
•    Required: Possess high school diploma or equivalent. (Higher degree would be a plus)
•    Required: Be able to perform basic mathematical calculations.
•    Required: Possess the ability to prioritize and multitask in a fast paced environment.
•    Required: Have a basic understanding of an open pit and heap leach mining process.
•    Previous experience in the Maintenance Health (Maintenance Dispatcher) field is a benefit but not required.
•    Has moderate abilities using basic Microsoft computer applications (Excel, Word, Outlook and MS Project) and can navigate through network drives to access folders.
•    Strong communication skills.
•    Ability to work with minimum supervision.
•    Demonstrated history of working with others, displaying a positive attitude, and working as part of a team.
•    Satisfactory Performance, attendance, and safety record.
•    Demonstrated ability to manage confidential information.
•    Ability to work with others in a team environment.
•    Willing to develop skills in other areas of responsibility within the Mobile Maintenance Department.
•    Understands mining and maintenance processes and communicates with the various departments as needed.
•    Provide Accurate equipment location list to planning department.
•    Knowledge of maintenance crew members and their abilities.
•    Well versed in mining equipment and equipment operations.
•    Must be able to help troubleshoot equipment problems and guide operators over the radio in a professional manner.
•    Manage the phone, radio and computer duties in Dispatch such as:
     Understand code blue procedures and responsibilities.
     Understand Maintenance Organizational charts and resources available.
     Other tasks as assigned.
•    Develop understanding of Dispatch systems and capability of running the system:
     Understand how to call equipment down and properly reason coding.
     Understand how to call equipment up and properly reason coding.
     Understand the overall equipment efficiency (OEE) standards for Mobile Equipment.
•    Develop understanding of Machine Health Systems and capability of running the system:
     Understand how to extract information.
     Understand how to plot charts and identify potential issues.
     Creating Pre-PM reports.
     Quickly react to critical alarms and/or reoccurring events.
•    Develop an understanding of JDE Maintenance module and gain the skills needed to efficiently utilize the system:
      Creating work orders.
      Requesting stock parts.
      Properly coding Work Orders.
      Create pre-ops Follow-up work orders
•    Being able to generate basic excel based reports.
•    Must be able to handle basic optimization and communicate in a timely manner.
•    Request assistance from supervision/management based on events when required.

jobs.title: Mine Engineer (Elko, NV, US)
jobs.description:
Bald Mountain is an open-pit mine with a large estimated mineral resource in the largest private mining land package in the U.S. The mine is located in White Pine County, one of the best mining jurisdictions in the world, along the southern extension of the prolific Carlin trend. Bald Mountain and the nearby Round Mountain mine make up Kinross’ Nevada operations. 

Bald Mountain is an important contributor to the economy of northeastern Nevada and maintains a comprehensive environmental strategy including wildlife protection, habitat recovery and education.

Job Summary

Under the direction of the Senior Mine Engineer or their designee, this person performs engineering tasks. They are to use engineering first principles to contribute to the design, and development of processes, practices, and methodologies within the Technical Services Group. They are to coordinate activities related to a full-range of engineering functions, and ensure achievement of service/operating standards (internally/externally).  They must be willing to work in a fast-paced, dynamic environment where they can apply their engineering knowledge and skills to create solutions to operational challenges.  

Essential Functions

1. Responsibilities may be focused in one of the following areas of engineering: short- and long-term mine planning, project controls, cost controls, construction, geotechnical, environmental, production, exploration or continuous improvement 
2.  Integrates short-term plans into long-term, and life-of-mine plans.
3.  Analyzes and interprets mine plans to ensure alignment with operational objectives.
4.  Must be willing to take on cross-rotation assignments within the Technical Services Group for personal development.
5.  Independently handles relevant technical duties, including application submittal, monitoring, and reporting.
6.  Researches information to support decision-making and improve processes, technologies or methodologies.
7.  Contributes to the development of policies and practices.
8.  Monitors costs related to services provided, and implements approved recommendations for maximizing operational efficiencies.
9.  Maintains excellent rapport with external regulatory agencies to foster working relationships that minimize adversarial actions and maximizes information exchange.
10.  Conducts regular and frequent inspections of operations / equipment / processes / procedures to ensure planned production goals can be met and regulatory / permit compliance.
11.  Responds to a variety of internal and / or external requests.
12.  Prepares communication materials, manuals and other written materials related to technical issues, programs, or systems including technical reports and documentation to ensure compliance with regulatory / industry and operational requirements.

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

1. B.S. Degree in Mining or Engineering Related.
2.  1-3 Years’ experience in surface mining preferred.
3.  Comprehensive knowledge of the principles and concepts of open pit mining engineering.  
4.  General understanding of mining operations, as well as limited understanding of heap leach operations.
5.  Working knowledge of computer-aided mine design and familiarity with one or more commercial software packages (Deswik, Vulcan, etc.) is preferred.
6.  Proficiency in MS Office suite of software (Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
7.  Requires technical communication skills, as well as, strong interpersonal skills (written/ verbal and analytical/ persuasive).
8.  Must be able to communicate effectively with all levels of staff and management.
9.  Ability to learn quickly and to function within the physical demand requirements.
10.  Understanding of Kinross’ processes and corporate values is an asset.
11.  Ability to work independently and as a member of the Engineering Team. 
12.  Must be 18 years old and presently authorized to work in the United States on a full time basis. 
13.  Requires valid driver’s license.

Health, Safety, and Environmental Requirements

 1. Adheres to all safety and environmental considerations.
 2. Have a strong commitment to safe working practices. 
 3. Wears Personal Protective Equipment at all times while in the production environment. 
 4. Is alert and observes, corrects, and reports unsafe conditions. 
 5. Follows operating procedures and complies with all regulatory requirements. 

Kinross Competencies

•  Strategic Effectiveness
Developing and communicating rigorous and creative business strategies that drive sustainable value.
•  External Engagement
Understanding and building relationships with external parties that strengthen and sustain competitive advantage.
•  Business Focus
Applying commercial rigor and discipline to all business decisions and customer relationships.
•  Living the Kinross Values
Aligning behavior, decisions, and actions with Kinross values and principles.

Legislative Requirements

Background Check required

US work permit required

Language Requirements

English

jobs.title: MEM Supervisor (Fairbanks, AK, US)
jobs.description:
Located approximately 26 miles from the City of Fairbanks, Fort Knox is a centre of excellence for the Company as one of the few cold weather heap leach facilities in the world.

Fort Knox

celebrated its 25-year anniversary

in 2021, and has produced over 8.5 million ounces since it began operation. In 2020, Kinross acquired Manh Choh – a project expected to commence production in 2024 and process ore at Fort Knox.

Fort Knox prioritizes being a strong contributor to the State and local communities, and since 2001, has helped support more than 300 community partners and has contributed more than US$25 million to the Alaska Mental Health Trust.

Job Description

Provide complex technical support to Mobile Maintenance. To follow established policies, practices, and procedures when completing work assignments. Supervise and instruct Mobile Maintenance shift crew activities to maximize Mobile Maintenance efficiencies in a safety-oriented workplace and meet production goals.

Job Responsibilities

Direct the activities of mechanics.

Work with Mobile Maintenance General Foreman and Maintenance Planner to plan and schedule daily work.

Assist the planner in determining technical specifications of equipment.

Interface with various equipment manufacturers’ representatives.

Work closely with Mine Supervisor to help meet production goals.

Monitor work areas on an ongoing basis to assure safe and cost efficient maintenance goals.

Investigate, analyze, and supervise the documentation of accidents, injuries, and equipment damage.

Report processing: daily time cards, vacation schedules, injury reports, accident reports, and disciplinary action.

Maintenance of a daily log of work assignments and accomplishments.

Prevent needless expenditures and lost production by minimizing equipment downtime through properly executed preventative maintenance and repairs.

Review documentation of accidents, injuries and equipment damage and recommend prevention strategies as necessary.
Maintain accurate records and files.

Consistent exercise of discretion and judgment in job performance.

Responsible for conducting and doing performance evaluations, recommending promotions, and carrying out corrective actions as needed.

Punctuality and regular attendance is required.
Meet or exceed established performance expectations set by management.
Compliance with all company policies and procedures including, but not limited to, safety, confidentiality, and environmental policies.
Possession of a valid driver’s license issued by the state.
Work safely in all areas, identify potential safety hazards, and work with management to correct hazards.
Work without significant risk of harm to self and others.
Perform other duties as required.

Education and Experience

Education
• High school diploma or equivalent preferred.  Employee must have sufficient education to read and write instructions, perform simple mathematical calculations, and keep records.

Experience

Three years’ experience in repairing and maintaining heavy equipment.

A minimum of two years’ experience as a supervisor or relief supervisor.

Skills

Experience with computerized maintenance systems.

Master mechanic's troubleshooting ability.

Strong working knowledge of diesel, gasoline, electronic, hydraulic, and welding equipment.

Thorough understanding of the maintenance requirements and procedures for heavy mobile equipment is necessary.

Must be production orientated.

Good working knowledge and skill with a P.C. utilizing word processing and spreadsheet programs.

Must have solid verbal and written communication skills.

Must be a self-starter with the ability to work independently, with others in a team environment, and also as a member of the management team.

Ability to function within the qualifications outlined in the attached physical demands sheets.

May work holidays, shift work, and weekends as required.

Reporting Relationships

This role reports to the MEM General Supervisor. 

Legislative Requirements

US work permit required

Language Requirements

English

Travel Requirements

Travel not required, only exceptionally

jobs.title: Warehouse Supervisor (Round Mountain, NV, US)
jobs.description:
Round Mountain is an open-pit mine located in Nevada, one of the best mining jurisdictions in the world. The mine uses conventional open-pit mining methods and processes ore by mill and heap leach. Kinross began operating the mine in 2003, and it has since become a continuous improvement leader in the Company’s portfolio. Round Mountain poured its 15 millionth ounce in 2018. Round Mountain and the nearby Bald Mountain mine make up Kinross’ Nevada operations. 

The Round Mountain mine is an important contributor to the Nye County economy and, working with local stakeholders, has helped achieve significant improvements in healthcare and education in the area.

Job Summary

Under the direction of the Supply Chain Superintendent, maintains appropriate levels of inventory, recommends re-orders, assures material is stored in a secure manner, and directs personnel in the receiving, stocking, and issuance of materials and directs inventory control.  Maintain records of all warehouse operations.  Assists in all warehouse functions to include the operation of all materials handling equipment while continuously aligning daily functions to reflect Kinross’ values. 

Essential Functions

1.  Ensure that the material received in the warehouse is equal in quantity and quality to that which is purchased and that it is available in the shortest possible time.
2.  Plan, organize, and implement the general layout of the warehouse, making changes as necessary.
3.  Administer warehouse operations to ensure effective daily operation.
4.  Ensure that all materials are stored safely and securely.
5.  Ensure that materials are issued or credited to users in an accurate and timely manner.
6.  Maintain and safeguard all materials stored in the warehouse.
7.  Oversees all inventory is stored on site for two equipment maintenance contractors.
8.  Compliance with all company policies and procedures including, but not limited to safety, environmental, confidentiality and code of conduct. 
9.  Meets or exceeds established performance expectations set by management.
10.  Consistently exercises discretion and judgment in job performance.
11.  Works without risk or harm to self and others. 
12.  Punctuality and regular attendance required.
13.  Helps develop other department personnel to perform duties listed above.
14.  Performs other related functions as assigned by supervisor.

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

1.  Must be able to work on materials management computer systems.
2.  Ability to supervise employees.
3.  Ability to analyze and solve problems.
4.  Knowledge of mining equipment and materials.
5.  Knowledge of inventory and warehouse functions. 
6.  A minimum of 4 years’ experience in Warehouse Management Supervisor position preferred.
7.  4-6 years’ experience in Materials Management Systems, i.e. JD Edwards, Mincom or SAP preferred
8.  Possesses good communication and interpersonal skills. 
9.  General understanding of mining operations, as well as limited understanding of milling and maintenance operations.
10.  Working knowledge and skill with P.C. utilizing word processing, spreadsheet, database, and presentation software. 
11.  Strong verbal, written, analytical and persuasive skills and the ability to interact effectively with all levels of employees and management.
12.  Demonstrate strong administrative, organizational and technical writing skills.
13.  Must be 18 years old and presently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. 
14.  Requires valid driver’s license.

Health, Safety, and Environmental Requirements

•    Adheres to all safety and environmental considerations.
•    Have a strong commitment to safe working practices. 
•    Wears Personal Protective Equipment at all times while in the production environment. 
•    Is alert and observes, corrects, and reports unsafe conditions. 
•    Follows operating procedures and comply with all regulatory requirements. 

Kinross Leadership Practices

•  Create an environment where nothing is more important than every employee returning home safe and healthy every day.  
•  Creates an environment in which people are unfailingly treated with respect. 
•  Fosters the talent and potential of all employees by enabling them to grow, develop, and make a difference in the organization. 
•  Demonstrates that leadership in the areas of environmental performance and community and stakeholder relations is fundamental to the way we plan and manage our business.  
•  Holds self and others accountable for the decisions, commitments, and behaviors required to deliver outstanding results. 
•  Uses judgment to manage business complexities, prioritize and balance conflicting demands to make timely decisions that best advance Kinross strategy.  
•  Builds and brings teams and people together to achieve organizational goals.  Models humility by going beyond self-interest for the good of the group.
•  Understands the economic implications of decisions and consistently uses all resources effectively and efficiently to maximize shareholder value. 
•  Relentlessly champions, develops and embeds best practices.  

Kinross Competencies

•  Strategic Effectiveness
Developing and communicating rigorous and creative business strategies that drive sustainable value.
•  External Engagement

Act as a member of the senior management team to develop the overall Business Support strategy and operating plans for the department.

Ensure financial transactions are recorded accurately and in compliance with Kinross, Great Bear standards and regulations.

.

Develop and implement expense management policies that are aligned with Kinross, Great Bear standards, ensuring site-wide compliance and clear communication with employees.

Coordinate with corporate finance teams on reporting, audits, and financial controls.

Work in a healthy work environment with full support, cooperation, and commitment to satisfy our operation’s goal of being accident-free.

Round Mountain is an open-pit mine located in Nevada, one of the best mining jurisdictions in the world. The mine uses conventional open-pit mining methods and processes ore by mill and heap leach. Kinross began operating the mine in 2003, and it has since become a continuous improvement leader in the Company’s portfolio. Round Mountain poured its 15 millionth ounce in 2018. Round Mountain and the nearby Bald Mountain mine make up Kinross’ Nevada operations. 

The Round Mountain mine is an important contributor to the Nye County economy and, working with local stakeholders, has helped achieve significant improvements in healthcare and education in the area.

Job Summary

We are seeking a motivated, collaborative, and proactive Human Resources Business Partner (HRBP) to join our Human Resources team. Our team has one open role, and we are seeking a mid-level or senior-level candidate. As a trusted advisor, the HRBP partners with leaders to provide strategic and operational HR guidance that supports business objectives, strengthens employee engagement, and fosters a positive, high-performing workplace. This role exercises a high degree of independent judgment in assessing employee relations matters, conducting workplace investigations, interpreting Company policy, and recommending practical, business-focused solutions.

This position balances strategic partnership with hands-on execution. Responsibilities include coaching leaders, managing employee relations issues, conducting workplace investigations, supporting workforce planning and organizational initiatives, and overseeing key HR programs—including company housing, onboarding, employee lifecycle activities, and compliance. Success in this role requires strong decision-making, sound judgment, relationship-building skills, adaptability, and a customer-focused approach in a fast-paced environment.

This is a full-time, on-site position based at Round Mountain Gold Corporation. The typical work schedule is Monday - Thursday, 10-hour shifts, with occasional flexibility required to meet business and operational needs.

Essential Functions

Serves as a trusted business partner to leaders by providing proactive HR consultation, coaching, and guidance aligned with business objectives.

Analyzes workforce trends, metrics, and organizational data to identify opportunities and develop practical solutions that support business goals.

Supports leaders in resolving employee relations matters and conducts prompt, thorough, and objective workplace investigations.

Maintains a strong working knowledge of employment laws, regulations, and Company policies while advising leaders to reduce organizational risk and ensure compliance.

Supports drug and alcohol program, including test administration support as needed.

Coaches leaders on employee performance, accountability, career development, conflict resolution, corrective action, employee engagement, and talent development.

Provides HR policy guidance and interpretation while ensuring consistent application of Company policies and practices.

Partners with leaders to support organizational change initiatives and assists with change management planning and implementation.

Participates in leadership development initiatives by supporting succession planning, talent reviews, workforce planning, and employee development efforts.

Partners with leaders and employees to strengthen working relationships, improve engagement and retention, and lead HR projects and continuous improvement initiatives that enhance operational effectiveness.

Administers day-to-day HR programs and employee lifecycle activities, including onboarding, transfers, promotions, compensation changes, leaves of absence, separations, HRIS updates, documentation, reporting, and compliance requirements while identifying opportunities to improve processes and service delivery.

Supports recruiting activities, onboarding, employee engagement initiatives, recognition programs, community outreach events, and new hire orientation as needed.

Assists leaders with workforce planning, organizational design, staffing strategies, and department restructures to support business needs.

Maintains accurate employee information and utilizes HR systems to prepare reports, analyze trends, and support informed business decisions.

Assists with audits, compliance activities, reporting requirements, and documentation to ensure adherence to Company policies and applicable regulations.

Coordinates Company housing and other assigned HR programs, ensuring effective administration and a positive employee experience.

Maintains confidentiality while handling sensitive employee information and business matters.

Complies with all Company policies and procedures, including but not limited to safety, environmental, confidentiality, and the Company's Code of Conduct.

Performs other related duties and special projects as assigned.

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

Must have 1-3 years' experience in a HR related role, with a focus on resolving employee related issues. 

Progressively responsible Human Resources experience supporting leaders in employee relations, performance management, investigations, and organizational initiatives.

Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or a related field preferred. An equivalent combination of education and experience will be considered.

General understanding of mining, industrial, manufacturing, or other heavy industry environments preferred.

Working knowledge of multiple Human Resources disciplines, including employee relations, performance management, compensation, talent development, organizational effectiveness, workforce planning, and federal and state employment laws.

Experience conducting workplace investigations and providing guidance on employee relations matters.

Demonstrated ability to build strong relationships and influence others.

jobs.title: Underground Chief Engineer (Round Mountain, NV, US)
jobs.description:
Round Mountain is an open-pit mine located in Nevada, one of the best mining jurisdictions in the world. The mine uses conventional open-pit mining methods and processes ore by mill and heap leach. Kinross began operating the mine in 2003, and it has since become a continuous improvement leader in the Company’s portfolio. Round Mountain poured its 15 millionth ounce in 2018. Round Mountain and the nearby Bald Mountain mine make up Kinross’ Nevada operations. 

The Round Mountain mine is an important contributor to the Nye County economy and, working with local stakeholders, has helped achieve significant improvements in healthcare and education in the area.

Job Summary

Kinross Round Mountain is a leading mining company dedicated to sustainable and safe mining practices. We are committed to innovation and excellence in all our operations. Join our team to contribute to challenging and rewarding projects in a dynamic and supportive environment. Round Mountain is renowned as one of the most geotechnically challenging mines in Nevada.

Our Round Mountain Technical Services team is seeking an experienced Chief Underground Mining Engineer to lead the underground tech services group comprising of mine engineers, planners, surveyors, ventilation engineers, and technical technicians for the Underground Mine at Round Mountain Gold Mine. Reporting to the UG Technical Services Manager, you will ensure that the mine’s long-hope stoping mining method is designed, scheduled, and executed safely and profitably. This role will also act as the primary technical liaison between operations, geology, and management. The underground is currently in its early development stages and now transitioning from exploration development to capital development. This is a great opportunity for a motivated individual to build the foundation for the underground mining engineering group, standards, and procedures that will be used for the life of mine.  

Qualified candidates may be eligible for both a sign-on bonus and relocation assistance.

Essential Functions

• Mine Planning & Design
Develop and oversee short , mid , and long range mine plans for a long hole stoping operation using paste backfill and cemented rockfill. Approve stope designs, drill patterns, sequencing, and ground support strategies. Ensure backfill requirements (strength, timing, curing windows) are integrated into the mine schedule. Optimize stope sequencing to balance geotechnical stability, ventilation constraints, and production targets
• Technical Leadership & Team Management
Lead, mentor, and develop mine engineers, surveyors, and technical staff. Foster a collaborative environment between engineering and operations, emphasizing problem solving and continuous improvement. Set technical standards, review engineering work, and ensure quality control across all engineering deliverables.
• Operational Support
Provide real time technical guidance to underground operations, including drilling, blasting, backfilling, and ground support installation. Troubleshoot stope performance issues (dilution, overbreak, paste delivery, drilling accuracy). Coordinate with maintenance, backfill plant personnel, and production supervisors to ensure alignment with engineering plans
• Safety, Regulatory, and Environmental Compliance
Ensure all engineering designs comply with MSHA regulations and Nevada state mining requirements. Support and reinforce site Health & Safety Management Systems and environmental compliance programs. Lead risk assessments for new stopes, mining methods, or ground conditions.
• Backfill & Geotechnical Integration
Work closely with geotechnical engineers to ensure stope stability, pillar design, and sequencing meet safety and production needs. Oversee paste backfill and CRF design parameters, QA/QC, and scheduling to maintain mine stability and minimize dilution.

• Budgeting & Project Management
Manage engineering department budgets, staffing, and capital project planning. Lead or support underground capital projects (ventilation upgrades, dewatering systems, new development headings, backfill plant improvements). Evaluate and justify new technologies, equipment, or software to improve efficiency.
• Data Management & Reporting
Oversee production reporting, stope reconciliation, and variance analysis. Ensure accurate survey control, mine modeling, and engineering databases. Present engineering updates to senior leadership and contribute to life of mine planning.

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

•    Bachelor’s degree in Mining Engineering or related field
•    8-15+ years of experience in underground hard-rock mining experience, with significant exposure to long-hole stoping
•    Demonstrated experience with paste backfill and CRF operations
•    Prior leadership or superintendent-level experience in technical services
•    Proficient in mine planning software – Deswik experience required
•    Knowledge of MSHA regulations and site safety practices
•    Proficient in Microsoft Software
•    Strong understanding of geotechnical principles, stope design, and backfill engineering
•    Familiarity with ventilation modeling, survey practices, and underground infrastructure design
•    Strong communication and cross-departmental coordination abilities
•    Ability to coach and mentor engineers at various experience levels
•    Strategic thinking with a focus on safety, efficiency, and long-term value creation
•    Requires a valid driver’s license.

Health, Safety, and Environmental Requirements

•    Adheres to all safety and environmental considerations.
•    Have a strong commitment to safe working practices. 
•    Wears Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) at all times while in the production environment. 
•    Is alert and observes, corrects, and reports unsafe conditions. 
•    Follows operating procedures and complies with all regulatory requirements.

jobs.title: Short Range Mine Engineer (Round Mountain, NV, US)
jobs.description:
Round Mountain is an open-pit mine located in Nevada, one of the best mining jurisdictions in the world. The mine uses conventional open-pit mining methods and processes ore by mill and heap leach. Kinross began operating the mine in 2003, and it has since become a continuous improvement leader in the Company’s portfolio. Round Mountain poured its 15 millionth ounce in 2018. Round Mountain and the nearby Bald Mountain mine make up Kinross’ Nevada operations. 

The Round Mountain mine is an important contributor to the Nye County economy and, working with local stakeholders, has helped achieve significant improvements in healthcare and education in the area.

Job Summary

The Mine Engineer I reports to the Senior Mine Engineer and is responsible for carrying out a full range of engineering functions including, but not limited to: mine planning, leach stacking plans, drill pattern design, drill and blast scheduling, blast pattern design, pit designs, stockpile, road and dump designs, mine analysis and production reporting. Will have direct involvement and communication with staff from other departments (Geology, Geotechnics, Maintenance and Operations).
Qualified candidates may be eligible for both a sign-on bonus and relocation assistance.

Essential Functions

1.  Develop and communicate engineering plans, technical reports and presentations, sequences, dumping priorities, etc. to Mine Operations and other stakeholders on site and ensure plans are carried out safely and efficiently 
2.  Leading pit tour with mine operations, supporting mine operations on the daily production meeting.
3.  Working on optimizing and improving the short-range planning processes
4.  Develop weekly mine plan, weekly mill feed strategy and perform a weekly mine plan adherence.  
5.  Drill and Blast Planning and Scheduling 
6.  Utilize geological data, mine plans and survey information to develop blast designs and shot timing, and release patterns as required for execution.
7.  Consult and develop a close working relationship with the Geotechnical Engineer in order to optimize pit wall stability.
8.  Perform accurate Drill/Blast pattern design duties on time - Preparation and Implementation of a Weekly Drill and Blast Plan.
9.  Perform pit design, dump design and infrastructure/road design.
10.  Identify risks (production and mine movement, equipment priorities, geotech, dewatering, grade, manpower, etc.) and opportunities that may impact the mine plans.
11.  Ensure information flow and buy-in to the mine plan process from various departments (load and haul, drill and blast, processing, etc).
12.  Collect and interpret technical data such as blast-induced vibration and utilize findings to inform pattern design decisions and improvements, with specific focus on high-risk sectors of the open pit.
13.  Safety Performance & Record, perform field engagement and risk identifications.
14.  Ensure drill & blast planning complies with applicable safety regulations, environmental standards, standard operating procedures and company best practices.
15.  Promote and engage strongly with a pro-active safety culture.

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

1.  Bachelor’s degree in Mining Engineering or similar field is required.
2.  1-5 years of planning and/or drill & blast experience in hard-rock, open pit mine operations is strongly preferred.
3.  Proficiency with mining software packages (Deswik, AutoCAD, Vulcan, MineSite) is strongly preferred.
4.  Working knowledge of mine operations and drill & blast principles.
5.  Comfortable working collaboratively in a team environment.
6.  Strong engagement with technical details, self-motivated to learn and continuously improve our mine planning and drill & blast practices.
7.  Must be presently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. 
8.  Valid driver’s license is required.

Health, Safety, and Environmental Requirements

•    Adheres to all safety and environmental regulations.
•    Has a strong commitment to safe working practices. 
•    Wears Personal Protective Equipment at all times while in the production environment. 
•    Is alert and observes, corrects, and reports unsafe conditions. 
•    Follows operating procedures and complies with all regulatory requirements. 

Legislative Requirements

Background Check required

US work permit required

Language Requirements

English

jobs.title: Intermediate Instrumentation & Control Engineer (Red Lake, ON, CA)
jobs.description:
The Great Bear project is a development-stage asset located in the renowned and prolific Red Lake mining district, and represents one of the most exciting recent gold discoveries globally.  The project has excellent potential to become a top-tier deposit that could support a large, long-life mine complex. Kinross’ comprehensive exploration and development program will aim to support the vision of a quality, high-grade, open-pit mine and a longer-term, sizeable underground mine.

Job Summary

The Intermediate Instrumentation and Control Engineer will assist the Instrumentation and Control Lead with engineering review of the instrumentation and control related work associated with the Great Bear Project, in particular process plant instrumentation and process control, utilities, water management instrumentation and process control, mining services and other infrastructure on surface and underground during Detailed Engineering.

Key Responsibilities and Duties

Conduct thorough reviews of vendor documents and comment on a wide range of technical documents including process functional descriptions, control narratives, PFDs and P&IDs, and selection of instrumentation for various applications for the Great Bear Project.

Ensure that the engineering design meets project specifications, safety standards, and regulatory requirements.

Provide feedback and recommend modifications to optimize design efficiency and functionality.

Oversee key engineering deliverables of I&C consultants in design offices and work of contractors on-site.

Ensure consultants and contractors adhere to project timelines, budgets, and quality standards.

Coordinate with consultants and contractors to resolve any issues or challenges that arise during detailed design, construction, and commissioning.

Collaborate with cross-functional teams of consultants, contractors, vendors, and work closely with the Great Bear Project team to ensure quality engineering deliverables regarding safety in design, constructability and cost.

Conduct required inspections and audits of I&C design, manufacturing, and installations.

Ensure compliance with safety regulations and best practices.

Maintain detailed records of all I&C engineering activities.

Prepare and submit regular reports to lead engineers.

Document any design changes, modifications, or issues encountered.

Maintain meeting minutes, project decisions, risk/issue trackers, and follow-ups with project stakeholders.

Work in a healthy work environment with full support, cooperation, and commitment to satisfy our operation’s goal of being accident-free.

Comply with federal and provincial acts and regulations, and legal requirements.

Support a work environment that is aligned with Kinross’ Safeground principles.

Adhere to all relevant Great Bear policies and procedures.

Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

A bachelor's degree in electrical, electronics, or control system engineering is required. A Professional Engineer designation in Ontario, or eligibility to obtain one, is preferred; however equivalent experience may be considered. A minimum of 5-10 years of relevant work experience is required. 

Familiar with industrial automation communication protocols (Modbus, EithernetIP, ProfiNet, Canopen), in addition to standard TCP/IP network skills.

Knowledge of industrial safety systems, such as LOPA, ATEX/IECEx zoning.

Familiarity with modern Process Control and Automation methods including Advance Process Control (APC), Ventilation on Demand (VOD), Analytics, simulation tools, Digital Twin and AI tools.

Experience with specification, startup, and troubleshooting of process control systems on hybrid environment using process control with DCS and high-level integration of vendor PLC applications to DCS, Power Management Systems and SCADA systems.

Knowledge of codes, standards, and regulations related to instrumentation and control systems, such as ISA, ANSI/IEEE, IEC, CEC and NEC, NFPA.

Hands-on programming experience of popular PLCs and DCS systems will be an added advantage.

Good understanding of mining and associated infrastructure, particularly in cold weather environments.

Familiarity with gold or similar mineral processing and exposure in engineering and commissioning.

Experience with automation engineering aspects of projects of varying scope and complexity from planning to execution.

Benefits

At Kinross, Great Bear, we are committed to Putting People First by fostering employee growth and development, celebrating achievements, and rewarding team success. Benefits offered for this position include: 

Annual Fitness and Mental Health Reimbursement 

Employee Share Purchase Plan, Registered Retirement Savings, and Registered Pension Plans

160 hours of Paid Vacation

Employee Assistance Program

Employee Recognition Program (Living our Values Award Program)

Health, Dental, and Vision Insurance

Life, Accidental Death & Dismemberment, and Disability Insurance

Training and Development Opportunities

Relocation assistance may be provided to eligible candidates on a case-by-case basis

Work Conditions

This position is based in Red Lake, Ontario. Local candidates, or those willing to relocate with relocation assistance, will be given priority for this position. The schedule is 5X2. Remote candidates may also be considered for this opportunity; however, relocation to Red Lake will be required by mid 2028. Frequent travel may be required.

Compensation and Total Rewards

The base salary range for the Intermediate Instrumentation and Control Engineer is $95,000 to $118,000 + Short Term Incentive Bonus, + Group Benefit Coverage. 

The hiring range reflects our targeted compensation framework for the role. jobs.title: Process Maintenance Mechanic (Round Mountain, NV, US)
jobs.description:
Round Mountain is an open-pit mine located in Nevada, one of the best mining jurisdictions in the world. The mine uses conventional open-pit mining methods and processes ore by mill and heap leach. Kinross began operating the mine in 2003, and it has since become a continuous improvement leader in the Company’s portfolio. Round Mountain poured its 15 millionth ounce in 2018. Round Mountain and the nearby Bald Mountain mine make up Kinross’ Nevada operations. 

The Round Mountain mine is an important contributor to the Nye County economy and, working with local stakeholders, has helped achieve significant improvements in healthcare and education in the area.

Job Description

Under the general supervision of the Process Maintenance Supervisor, the Maintenance Mechanic is responsible for performing preventative and corrective maintenance on all plant equipment, including milling, crushing, conveying, flotation, leaching, thickeners, gravity spirals, CICs, elution, refining, pumping, piping, and all supporting infrastructure. 

Job Responsibilities

1.    Perform mechanical maintenance, troubleshooting, diagnosis, and repair plant equipment including ADR systems, crushing circuits, milling circuits, and pumping/piping systems.
2.    Operate support equipment such as forklifts and overhead cranes.
3.    Perform bearing analysis and installation.
4.    Complete mechanical projects and fabrication work using basic cutting and welding techniques.
5.    Lubricate equipment, manage oil inventory, and ensure proper disposal of waste oil.
6.    Participate in preventative maintenance and capital/construction projects in coordination with operations and technical services.
7.    Respond to emergency maintenance calls on a 24-hour basis as required.
8.    Assist in the mentorship and training of other maintenance personnel and apprentices.
9.    Maintain accurate maintenance records and documentation for all work performed.
10.    Attend required classes and complete coursework and lab training as part of an apprenticeship (if enrolled).
11.    Comply with all company policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements, including those related to safety, environmental, and confidentiality.
12.    Exhibit regular attendance, punctuality, and the ability to work independently with minimal supervision.

Education and Experience

1.    High School Diploma or GED required.
2.    Minimum of 3 years of relevant maintenance experience in ADR and/or crusher systems preferred.
3.    Minimum of 3 years of relevant maintenance experience in an industrial setting required.
4.    Enrollment or completion of Millwright Apprenticeship Program preferred (including a minimum of 9 credit hours/semester and monthly lab work at Great Basin College).
5.    Knowledge of lubrication practices and mechanical systems.
6.    Skilled in basic welding and cutting
7.    Certified welding skills beneficial but not required
8.    Strong verbal, written, analytical, and interpersonal skills.
9.    Proficiency with computers and standard office software (Word, Excel, etc.).
10.    Ability to work effectively with cross-functional teams and all levels of personnel.
11.    Valid driver’s license.
12.    Ability to meet “Authorized User” requirements for High Risk Activities, including Fall Protection and Confined Space.

Reporting Relationships

Works under direct supervision of the Process Maintenance Supervisor.

Legislative Requirements

US work permit required

Background Check required

Language Requirements

English

jobs.title: Maintenance Supervisor - Haul & Support (Elko, NV, US)
jobs.description:
Bald Mountain is an open-pit mine with a large estimated mineral resource in the largest private mining land package in the U.S. The mine is located in White Pine County, one of the best mining jurisdictions in the world, along the southern extension of the prolific Carlin trend. Bald Mountain and the nearby Round Mountain mine make up Kinross’ Nevada operations. 

Bald Mountain is an important contributor to the economy of northeastern Nevada and maintains a comprehensive environmental strategy including wildlife protection, habitat recovery and education.

Job Summary

Under the general supervision of the Maintenance General Supervisor, the incumbent is responsible to ensure a safe, efficient, and productive work environment, while continuously aligning daily functions to reflect Kinross’ values and in compliance with Company policies. Leading by example in Safety, Attendance, Attitude and Performance.  

Essential Functions

Ensures that all planned maintenance activities for the shovel and drill fleets are properly executed in a safe and efficient manner. 

Develop maintenance assignments and assign crews to specific tasks to meet daily mine maintenance goals within the Kinross Way for Maintenance. 

Supervise crew activities during shifts to ensure safe and efficient accomplishment of assignments. 

Develop crew skills through task and special training to the levels of maximum efficiency and safety. 

Works with the planning department and other maintenance personnel to ensure that all parts, special tools, and equipment necessary to complete a planned task are available and accounted for before the job commences. 

Perform daily administrative duties such as time cards, reports, supply requisitions, effective safety meetings, environmental reports, safety inspections / reports, vacation schedules/ coverage time sheets, shift logs, perform work place inspections, perform daily work order management and manage daily workload.   

Maintain accurate and up to date records of work performed. Keeping daily schedules of both reactive and proactive work performed.  

Maintain a performance log on each of your reporting personnel. Ensure Personnel Evaluations are completed on time. 

This position is responsible for a staff of 5+ individuals, including mechanics, welders, electricians, and laborers. 

Responsible for crew training to include signing of the MSHA 5000-23 forms for all applicable jobs in the department.  

Must be able & willing to conduct weekly Safety Talks for the process group, and daily crew lineouts & any other assigned meetings. 

Ensure optimum use of facilities and equipment. Maintaining upkeep on all maintenance vehicles. 

Be a liaison with operations to plan, monitor, and execute planned maintenance, capital, and construction projects. Identify duration of maintenance or repair activity on equipment or facilities. 

Possesses good communication and interpersonal skills. Able to hold good relations with other department leaders. 

Help in the development of other department personnel to perform duties listed above.  

Consistently exercises discretion and judgment in job performance. Monitoring and evaluating job performances. 

Works without risk or harm to self and others. Always maintaining a Safety awareness.  

Promote and maintain Critical Risk Management (CRM) program. 

Must have general knowledge of company rules and policies so that decisions made are in conformance with company requirements. Schedule work assignments and prioritize crew activities in consultation with the General Supervisor. Guidance of crew members to ensure that a harmonious work environment is maintained when dealing with various personalities in the work force. 

Conduct accident or incident investigations. 

Keeps in active communication with the Maintenance General Supervisor, and periodically updates to him/her on the status of all work performed. 

Daily communication with the General Supervisor is required. Must ensure that he/she is immediately informed of important information, such as changes to the process, equipment problems, employee problems and incidents. 

Compliance with all company policies and procedures including, but not limited to safety, environmental, confidentiality and code of conduct.  

Meets or exceeds established performance expectations set by management. 

Punctuality and regular attendance required. 

Performs other related functions as assigned by supervisor. 

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

Must be able to operate JDE. 

Working knowledge and skill with P.C. utilizing word processing, spreadsheet, database, and presentation software. 

Minimum 5 years’ experience in Maintenance, preferable in a construction or mining environment.

Job Description

Under the general supervision of the Underground Maintenance Supervisor, the Underground Lube Technician is responsible for fueling, lubricating, and servicing underground mobile mining equipment to maximize equipment availability, reliability, and safe operation. jobs.description:
The Great Bear project is a development-stage asset located in the renowned and prolific Red Lake mining district, and represents one of the most exciting recent gold discoveries globally.  The project has excellent potential to become a top-tier deposit that could support a large, long-life mine complex. Kinross’ comprehensive exploration and development program will aim to support the vision of a quality, high-grade, open-pit mine and a longer-term, sizeable underground mine.

Job Summary

As the Superintendent, Site Services for the Great Bear Project you will provide leadership, planning, and overall accountability for the safe, reliable, and cost-effective delivery of site services. The role leads the operation, maintenance, and repair oversight of surface infrastructure, facilities and utilities, logistics, yard operations, waste management, water treatment, and associated maintenance activities, and provides direction to the Supervisor, Site Services internal crews, and contractors. Until the start of main project construction, you will oversee the maintenance and repair of site infrastructure, utilities, facilities, and non-core operational assets following handover from Project, supporting underground development and exploration including the operation of the 13km Chukuni Pipeline, worker camp and associated effluent treatment system. Upon project transition into full operations, you will assume full accountability for non-core operational assets following handover from Project.

Provide leadership, planning, and direction for site services team responsible for the operation and maintenance of the worker camp, yards, roads, utilities, logistics, site-wide waste management, and non-core infrastructure.

Develop and execute site services budgets, plans, preventative maintenance programs, and resource requirements in alignment with operational priorities. Support to the Projects team on an as-needed basis.

Establish and monitor service levels and key performance indicators for safety, environmental compliance, asset reliability, maintenance completion, cost, budget schedule; identify trends and implement corrective actions.

Provide oversight of contracts and contractors related to site services’ areas of responsibility.

Develop and implement contingency and business continuity planning for utility outages, equipment failures, severe weather, transportation disruptions, and other events that could affect site services.

Lead, coach, and hold accountable the Site Services Supervisor(s) and internal crews; establish clear roles, rotation handovers, staffing plans, training requirements, and performance expectations.

Participate in the development and execution of the Operational Readiness Plan for surface infrastructure, including maintenance strategies, procedures, staffing, training, spares, and service continuity.

Work in a healthy work environment with full support, cooperation, and commitment to satisfy our operation’s goal of being accident-free.

Support a work environment that is aligned with Kinross’ Safeground principles.

Comply with federal and provincial acts and regulations, and legal requirements.

Adhere to all relevant Great Bear policies and procedures.

Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

A minimum of 7–10 years of progressive experience in site services, facilities, infrastructure, maintenance, logistics, or related functions within mining, construction, or industrial environments, including 3-5 years in a supervisory or superintendent capacity.

Experience leading multidisciplinary teams and contractors in a remote operating environment, during the start up phase, is required. 

A technical diploma, trade certificate, or equivalent combination of education and experience in mining, mechanical systems, and/or facilities management is preferred.

Strong working knowledge of site services support equipment such as forklifts, skid steers, generators, etc.

Strong knowledge of carpentry, plumbing, electrical, and mechanical systems and maintenance best practices.

Knowledge of materials-handling practices, lifting and rigging requirements, and safe equipment operation.

Experience with contractor management and project execution in remote mining environments.

Ability to read, interpret, and apply operating manuals and procedures.

Benefits

At Kinross, Great Bear, we are committed to Putting People First by fostering employee growth and development, celebrating achievements, and rewarding team success. Benefits offered for this position include: 

Annual Fitness and Mental Health Reimbursement

Employee Share Purchase Plan, Registered Retirement Savings, and Registered Pension Plans

160 Hours of Paid Vacation

Employee Assistance Program

Employee Recognition Program

Health, Dental, and Vision Insurance

Life, Accidental Death & Dismemberment, and Disability Insurance

Training and Development Opportunities

Relocation assistance may be provided to eligible candidates on a case-by-case basis

Work Conditions

This position is based in Red Lake, Ontario. Local candidates, or those willing to relocate, with relocation assistance, will be given priority for this position. The schedule for this position is 14X14, 12 hour days. 

Compensation and Total Rewards

The hiring range reflects our targeted compensation framework for the role. The actual offer will be determined through a comprehensive evaluation of each candidate's experience, capabilities, and potential impact, along with consideration of internal equity, team structure, and benchmark market data for similar positions. jobs.description:
The Great Bear project is a development-stage asset located in the renowned and prolific Red Lake mining district, and represents one of the most exciting recent gold discoveries globally.  The project has excellent potential to become a top-tier deposit that could support a large, long-life mine complex. Kinross’ comprehensive exploration and development program will aim to support the vision of a quality, high-grade, open-pit mine and a longer-term, sizeable underground mine.

Job Summary

Under the guidance of the Chief Geologist, the Core Logging Geologists will be positive hard working team players who are passionate about geology and help to grow the Kinross – Great Bear project from generative exploration and drill targeting, through to resource delineation and grade control in the future Open Pit and Underground environments. Core Logging Geologists will work independently to better understand all geologic factors and bring forward ideas to further improve our understanding of the mineralized system and surrounding areas.

Key Responsibilities and Duties

The primary duty will be logging diamond drill core with an emphasis on recording lithology, structure mineralization and alteration. 

A geological interpretation may be required after each hole, or fan of logging is completed.

Fill-in for UG/OP Beat Geologists as necessary.

Work in a healthy work environment with full support, cooperation, and commitment to satisfy our operation’s goal of being accident-free.

A Bachelor of Science in Geology or Earth Sciences is required. Professional Geoscience or G.I.T is beneficial. There is no minimum experience requirement for this position; however, individuals with previous exploration experience is beneficial.

Experience with Leapfrog, or similar program is desired. 

Ability to plan drill holes and interpret results. 

Capable of learning and adapting to new equipment and software.

Comprehends and capable of interpreting technical language. 

High level of technical skills in MS Office (Word, Excel, Outlook).

This role ensures long-term strategic plans are economically optimized, safe, and compliant with geotechnical and environmental standards. Under the direction of the Underground Mobile Maintenance Supervisor, the Underground Mobile Maintenance Technician is responsible for safely inspecting, troubleshooting, servicing, and repairing underground mobile mining equipment in both shop and field environments. This role supports reliable production by maintaining loaders, haul trucks, drills, bolters, shotcrete and support equipment, with a strong focus on safety, equipment availability, diagnostic accuracy, and quality workmanship in a fast-paced underground mining operation.

Comply with all company policies, procedures, and applicable safety, environmental, and regulatory requirements, including underground mining standards and safe work practices. 

Inspect, troubleshoot, diagnose, and repair underground mobile equipment including loaders, haul trucks, drills, bolters, shotcrete equipment, utility vehicles, and other support equipment. 

Perform planned maintenance, component change-outs, breakdown repairs, and follow-up inspections in both underground field locations and shop settings. 

Troubleshoot hydraulic, electrical, mechanical, pneumatic, powertrain, and braking systems using schematics, manuals, onboard diagnostics, and technical support resources. 

Read and interpret service manuals, blueprints, parts information, and equipment schematics to complete accurate and efficient repairs. 

Complete detailed work orders, service reports, failure documentation, and parts requests with a high level of accuracy and timeliness. 

Maintain high housekeeping standards in work areas, service trucks, and shops to support a safe and efficient underground maintenance environment. 

Work closely with operations, planning, warehouse, and fellow maintenance team members to minimize downtime and support reliable production. 

Demonstrate ownership of assigned equipment, tools, and tasks while consistently meeting performance, attendance, and workmanship expectations. 

Support continuous improvement efforts, share technical knowledge with teammates, and assist in developing less experienced maintenance personnel. 

Perform other related duties as assigned by supervision in support of underground maintenance and production objectives.

Three (3) or more years of heavy equipment maintenance experience preferred, with underground mobile maintenance experience strongly preferred. 

Strong troubleshooting and repair skills in hydraulic, electrical, mechanical, and powertrain systems on underground mining equipment required. 

Experience maintaining underground equipment such as loaders, haul trucks, jumbos, bolters, drills, shotcrete units, and utility/support equipment preferred. 

Strong background in underground drilling and bolting equipment repair is highly preferred. 

Ability to read and interpret schematics, service manuals, technical bulletins, and parts information required. 

Experience with OEM diagnostic and service software is preferred. 

Diesel technology training, technical certification, or equivalent hands-on experience is preferred. 

Ability to safely operate support equipment including forklifts, skid steers, telehandlers, service trucks, and similar tools/equipment preferred. 

Strong communication, teamwork, and interpersonal skills with the ability to work effectively across maintenance and operations teams required. 

Ability to work independently, prioritize tasks, and perform effectively with limited supervision in a production-driven underground environment required. 

Strong computer skills for work order entry, equipment history review, and maintenance reporting preferred. 

Must have a proven commitment to safety, quality workmanship, and dependable attendance. 

Must be willing and able to work rotating shifts, including days, nights, weekends, holidays, overtime, and callouts as needed to support operations. 

Must be 18 years old and presently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. 

Valid driver’s license required. 

Skills

Must have sufficient mechanical knowledge. 

4-5 years of underground heavy equipment repair experience preferred.

jobs.description:
Round Mountain is an open-pit mine located in Nevada, one of the best mining jurisdictions in the world. The mine uses conventional open-pit mining methods and processes ore by mill and heap leach. Round Mountain and the nearby Bald Mountain mine make up Kinross’ Nevada operations. 

The Round Mountain mine is an important contributor to the Nye County economy and, working with local stakeholders, has helped achieve significant improvements in healthcare and education in the area.

Job Summary

Kinross Round Mountain is a leading mining company dedicated to sustainable and safe mining practices. We are committed to innovation and excellence in all our operations. Join our team to contribute to challenging and rewarding projects in a dynamic and supportive environment. Round Mountain is renowned as one of the most geotechnically challenging mines in Nevada.

Our Round Mountain Technical Services team is seeking a Underground Surveyor Supervisor to lead the Underground Survey group for the Underground Mine at Round Mountain Gold Mine. Reporting to the UG Chief Mine Engineer, you will lead the underground survey department, manage survey standards and quality control, and provide accurate, timely spatial data to engineering, geology, and operations. This role will ensure that all underground workings, long-hole stopes, and infrastructure are surveyed, mapped, and reported to support safe and efficient mining. The underground is currently in its early development stages and now transitioning from exploration development to capital development. This is a great opportunity for a motivated individual to build the foundation for the underground survey group, standards, and procedures that will be used for the life of mine.  

Qualified candidates may be eligible for both a sign-on bonus and relocation assistance.

•  Survey Leadership and Team Management
Lead, train, and develop the underground survey team, ensuring consistent technical performance and adherence to best practices. Assign daily and weekly survey tasks aligned with mine planning and production priorities. Maintain a culture of safety, accuracy, and continuous improvement within the survey group.
•  Underground Surveying and Data Collection
Establish and maintain underground survey control networks, including primary and secondary control points. Perform development surveys, including heading markups, line and grade, and breakthrough checks. Conduct production surveys for long hole stopes, including collaring, toe checks, and cavity monitoring. Capture as built data for development, infrastructure, and backfill operations.
•  Long-hole Stoping Support
Provide precise drill markups for long hole production drilling. Verify stope boundaries, slot raises, and breakthrough locations to minimize dilution and ensure compliance with design. Survey underground backfill boundaries to support geotechnical and engineering QA/QC.
•  Data Management and Reporting
Maintain accurate survey databases, digital models, and spatial records. Deliver timely updates to mine engineering, geology, and operations, including 3D models, maps, and progress reports. Support reconciliation of planned vs. actual development and stope performance on a regular cadence as needed (daily, weekly, monthly)
•  Technology, Equipment, and Quality Control
Oversee maintenance, calibration, and proper use of survey instruments (total stations, scanners, LiDAR, GPS for surface tie ins). Implement QA/QC procedures for all survey data and deliverables. Evaluate and adopt new survey technologies to improve accuracy and efficiency.

This role is responsible for leading crews, coordinating daily execution of development and production plans, maintaining compliance with MSHA, Nevada, environmental, and company standards, and building a culture where safety, accountability, communication, and operational excellence are consistently demonstrated. The UG Mine General Supervisor is expected to bring strong underground hard rock mining experience, sound judgment, effective employee leadership, and the ability to make timely decisions in a dynamic mining environment.

•  Partner with Maintenance to prioritize repairs, manage equipment downtime, coordinate availability of mobile and fixed assets, and support efficient execution of the mine plan.

The Process Control Engineer is responsible for developing, maintaining, and optimizing process control systems that support safe, reliable, and efficient mineral processing operations at the Round Mountain Gold Mine. This role focuses on improving plant stability, throughput, recovery, and equipment performance through effective control strategies, automation enhancements, and close collaboration with operations, metallurgy, and maintenance teams.

Qualified candidates may be eligible for both a sign-on bonus and relocation assistance.

Process Control & Automation
•    Design, implement, maintain, and optimize control strategies for crushing, grinding, classification, leaching, adsorption, detoxification, and ancillary systems as applicable.
•    Configure, troubleshoot, and support plant control systems (e.g., DCS, PLCs, HMI/SCADA) to ensure high system availability and reliability.
•    Develop and tune regulatory, advanced, and model-based control loops to improve process stability and metallurgical performance.
•    Lead and support control system upgrades, logic changes, alarm management, and interface improvements in accordance with site change management procedures.
Operational Support
•    Partner with Operations and Metallurgy to identify process constraints and variability, and implement control solutions that improve throughput, recovery, and reagent efficiency.
•    Provide on-shift and off-shift technical support for control system issues impacting production or safety.
•    Analyze process data and trends to proactively identify opportunities for improvement and risk mitigation.
Maintenance & Reliability Interface
•    Work closely with the Process Maintenance Superintendent and maintenance teams to support instrumentation, control hardware, and network reliability.
•    Support preventative maintenance strategies, control system documentation, and lifecycle management of automation assets.
•    Assist with root cause analysis for process upsets and equipment or control-related failures.
Safety, Compliance & Standards
•    Promote a strong safety culture by ensuring control systems support safe operating limits and critical safeguards.
•    Participate in hazard analyses, management of change (MOC), and operational readiness reviews.
Projects & Continuous Improvement
•    Provide process control expertise for capital projects, plant modifications, and technology trials.

•    Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives focused on cost reduction, energy efficiency, and operational excellence.

•    Process data analysis and visualization tools (e.g., Wonderware, PI System or equivalent historians).
